evidence.quoted_text:
"manager_restarted": (
            (((manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager") or {})
             .get("pid") or 0) > 0
            and (((manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                 .get("pid") or 0) > 0
            and (manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("pid")
            != (manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("pid")
            and bool(((manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                     .get("invocation_id"))
            and bool(((manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                     .get("invocation_id"))
            and (manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("invocation_id")
            != (manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("invocation_id")),
evidence.reason: The `manager_restarted` check compares only manager PID and invocation ID and never requires the before/after snapshots to share a nonempty boot ID. If the guest reboots between those snapshots, both PID and invocation ID can differ, so `manager_restarted` can pass without proving that the restart command itself caused the restart. The later reboot check can still pass using its own before/after snapshots. Requiring equal nonempty boot IDs in the manager snapshot pair is a small routine correctness fix; the existing PID and invocation ID checks should remain.
